cohort: 2155 mother-baby dyads from 17 counties in New York State with live births between 34-36 6/7 weeks gestation from 2010-2012
finding: Late preterm infants born to obese mothers were more likely to be delivered by cesarean section, have larger birth weights, and require assisted ventilation and NICU admission, especially for infants born to mothers with class III obesity.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher among obese mothers compared to mothers with normal BMI.
birth_weight: Increased birth weight in infants of obese mothers
